The fix: pick ONE thing you'll stop giving away. Texts after 7 PM. Skipped breaks. Every extra shift. Start this week, quietly.

slides.big: Every night you stay "just 20 more minutes," you give away time you'll never get paid for.
slides.small: And you still go home with nothing left.

Your shift ends at 5.
You walk out at 5:45.
Nobody asked you to stay.
Nobody thanks you either.

It feels safe.
If they ever cut people, maybe they'll remember you stayed.
So the job gets your best hours, and home gets what's left.

In Mental Health UK's Burnout Report 2026, 1 in 3 workers said they regularly work unpaid overtime.
It was the second biggest cause of work stress they named.

Pick your leave time.
Tell one person at home what it is.
Set an alarm 10 minutes before.
When it goes off, wrap up and walk out.

slides.big:
Staying late doesn't make you safe.
It makes you tired.

caption:
Working unpaid overtime at a job you can't afford to quit? 👇

Your shift ends at 5. You walk out at 5:45. Nobody asked you to stay. Nobody thanks you.

You stay because it feels safe, like they'll remember it if cuts come. So the job gets your best hours, and home gets what's left.

It's not just you. In Mental Health UK's Burnout Report 2026, 1 in 3 workers said they regularly work unpaid overtime, the second biggest cause of work stress they named.

The fix: pick a hard leave time, tell one person at home, and set an alarm. When it goes off, walk out.

How many free hours did YOU give this week? 👇
